items.title: A Very Thorough Appointment
items.text:
Mr. Li went to City Hospital with a small gash on his thumb and a wart on his finger. He sat on a gurney in the hallway. A nurse put a band-aid on the gash. She said the wart could wait. Mr. Li was glad. He had no phobia about hospitals. He just had other plans for the afternoon. The waiting room was busy. A poster offered acupuncture, hypnosis and psychoanalysis. Another poster said the hospital had a new ICU. Mr. Li did not need the ICU. He needed a doctor and maybe a cup of tea. The doctor arrived with a scalpel in his pocket. Mr. Li looked at the scalpel. He looked at his small wart. The doctor smiled. 'Do not worry,' he said. 'This is for later. Maybe much later.' Mr. Li hoped it was for never. The doctor washed his hands and put on clean gauze. He said, 'First, let us talk about your health.' Mr. Li said, 'It is a wart.' The doctor said, 'A wart is a good place to start.'

The doctor asked about Mr. Li's family history. Mr. Li said his father had anemia and a cataract. His mother had acne as a girl. His uncle had a tic and a mild palsy. His aunt had a cyst on her wrist. The doctor wrote everything down. He said Mr. Li might have a predisposition to some problems. He also said family history was not fate. Then he checked Mr. Li's lymph nodes. He looked for a blood clot. He said a clot could rupture, but Mr. Li's clot seemed fine. He asked about dizziness and vertigo. Mr. Li said he felt fine. The doctor asked about numbness and malaise. Mr. Li said he felt fine. The doctor asked about dehydration. Mr. Li said he had not had tea yet. The doctor said tea was a stimulant, not a cure. He gave Mr. Li a small balm for the wart. He said the balm was not a magic cure. It was a good start. He also said Mr. Li had no deformity and no sign of sclerosis. Mr. Li said, 'That is good news.' The doctor said, 'Yes. It is the best news I have given all morning.'

The doctor looked at the wart again. He said, 'We will not use morphine. Morphine is for serious pain. A wart is not serious pain. We will not use a catheter. We will not use dialysis. We will not use a ventilator or a respirator. We will not do a transplantation. We will not use the MRI today. The ICU is also not needed. We will use the balm and a band-aid.' Mr. Li was happy. He said, 'I like this plan.' The doctor said, 'There is one more thing. We must check for infection. We will use sterilization on the tools. We will clean the gash. A scab will form. That is normal. If the gash gets red, come back. Do not wait for a relapse. A relapse is not a good guest.' Mr. Li said, 'I will not wait.' The doctor nodded. He said, 'Also, avoid dehydration. Drink water. Avoid too much caffeine. Caffeine is a stimulant. It is not a food group.' Mr. Li said, 'I will drink water.' The doctor said, 'Good. Water is a fine balm for many small troubles.' Mr. Li said, 'You said balm already.' The doctor said, 'I like the word. It is short and calm. Unlike a relapse.'

Then the doctor began to talk about public health. He said epidemiology was the study of how diseases spread. He said cholera was rare here, but quarantine rules still mattered. He said immunization was important. It helped lower susceptibility to disease. He said malnutrition could cause growth retardation in children. It could also cause anemia and weakness. He said a carcinogen was something that could cause cancer. Smoking was a carcinogen. He said carcinoma and melanoma were serious skin problems. He said early checks helped. He said remission was good news. He said eradication of a disease was even better news. He said morbidity rates were falling. He said a small cut did not change that. Mr. Li said, 'I am glad.' The doctor said, 'You should be. Public health is a team sport. Today, your team is you, me, and a band-aid.'

The doctor said, 'One last thing. A skin graft is not needed for this gash. Your affliction is small. Your malady is even smaller. It is a wart. It is not a crisis.' Mr. Li said, 'Thank you.' The doctor said, 'You are welcome. Please do not worry about impotence from the balm. The balm does not cause impotence. It also does not cause amnesia. You will remember this visit. That may be the only side effect.' Mr. Li laughed. The doctor did not laugh. He said, 'We do not offer euthanasia here. We are not that kind of hospital. We do not offer hypnosis for warts either. We save that for something else.' Mr. Li said, 'I will come back if the wart gets worse.' The doctor said, 'Good. And if you feel dizzy, sit down. Dizziness is not a race.' Mr. Li left with a band-aid and a small bill. He felt fine. The doctor said aging and degeneration were normal. A wart was not a sign of either. Mr. Li had a wart and a story. He did not have a clot, a relapse, or a reason to return.

items.title: A Night at the Arts Center
items.text: Last weekend, my town held a small arts festival. A young singer opened the show. Then a musician played the piano. A poet read a short poem about the sea. A writer talked about her new book. An actor performed a funny scene. The producer of the event spoke to the audience. Many people were fans of one celebrity. They cheered loudly. After the show, we saw a new statue outside. It has a simple aesthetic. The festival showed that different aesthetics can live together. I enjoyed it very much.

items.title: A Simple Meal
items.text: A chef works in a small kitchen. He makes food for every meal. Today he cooks fish and an egg. He also makes a fruit jelly for dessert. He does not use much salt or sugar in his cooking. A vegan guest comes to the restaurant. She does not eat fish or eggs. The chef makes a plate of fresh vegetables for her. A waiter brings the plate to the table. The guest smiles and says the food is very good. The chef is happy. He likes to cook simple food. He wants every meal to taste nice.

items.title: A Good Meal at a Small Restaurant
items.text: My friend and I had a meal at a small restaurant. The chef cooked fish for me, and he cooked an egg for my other friend. He put the food on a white plate. I added a little salt, but no sugar. My friend is vegan, so she did not eat fish or eggs. The waiter brought her a fruit plate. It looked fresh and bright. For dessert, we shared some red jelly. The restaurant was quiet, and we could talk about our day. The food was simple, but very good. We paid and said thank you to the chef.

items.title: A Good Meal
items.text: Last night I went to a small restaurant for a meal. The chef cooked fish and an egg for me. I am not vegan, so I also ate some rice. The waiter brought my food on a clean plate. He also gave me a bowl of fruit. The fish was very good, but it needed a little salt. I did not want sugar on my fruit. For dessert, I had red jelly. Everything tasted fresh. The waiter was friendly. He asked if I liked the meal. I said yes. The chef came out and smiled. The food was simple but tasty. I will go back again.

items.title: A Week in the Hospital
items.text: Tom felt bad last week. He had pain in his stomach. He went to the hospital. A doctor did some tests. The blood test showed a problem. Tom was worried. The doctor said it was serious. Tom had cancer. At first, Tom was afraid. His family came to see him. He needed an operation. He stayed in bed for three days. The nurses gave him good care. He took his medicine every day. The treatment worked well. After some weeks, his health got better. He went back for a medical check. The doctor said he was fine. He was happy to go home.
